numerical_failure.observed_behavior: When `polyfit` is called with multiple right-hand sides (`y` with multiple columns / multiple `rhs`), the `cov=True` covariance output is not returned as one covariance matrix per `rhs`; instead it effectively uses only the first residual from `resids`, so only the first coefficients get a covariance matrix. The issue also describes the `C` return (when `cov=True, full=False`) as always having shape `(n, n, 1)` regardless of the shape of `y`.
numerical_failure.expected_behavior: Return one covariance matrix per `rhs` in `polyfit` (i.e., covariance should be computed for each set of coefficients corresponding to each `rhs`).
trigger_conditions: Calling `jax._src.numpy.polynomial.polyfit` with multiple right-hand sides (`y` has multiple columns / multiple `rhs`).

Specifically, when `resids` contains multiple residual values/rows (i.e., multiple `rhs`), using only the first residual from `resids` leads to covariance being computed only for the first set of coefficients.
oracle_clues: BUG: return one covariance matrix per `rhs` in `polyfit`.
Taking the first residual from `resids` means only the first set of coefficients would get a covariance matrix.
Issue statement: for `jax.numpy.polyfit` when `cov=True, full=False` the `C` return is always `(n, n, 1)`, regardless of the shape of `y`.
Fix description shows the intended behavior change around residual scaling/broadcasting across `y_arr` sizes for multiple `rhs` (e.g., expanding `fac` rather than indexing `fac[0]`).
Tests were extended with `num_rhs=[1, 5]` to cover single vs multiple `rhs` cases for `polyfit`.

category_specific_evidence: `jax.numpy.polyfit` with `cov=True` returns only one covariance matrix when `y` has multiple right-hand sides (multiple `rhs`).

From the issue example: with `x = np.arange(10).astype('float32')`, `num_rhs = 3`, and `y` shaped `(x.shape[0], num_rhs)`, `numpy.polyfit(x, y, 1, cov=True)[1]` returns an array with 3 covariance matrices (shape shown as `(3, 2, 2)` in the printed output).

In the same example, `jnp.polyfit(x, y, 1, cov=True)[1]` prints only 2 covariance matrices each with shape `(2, 1)` per printed slice, indicating that covariance output is not produced per `rhs` as expected; it “always [is] `(n, n, 1)`, regardless of the shape of `y`.”
The underlying code behavior described: “Taking the first residual from `resids` means that only the first set of coefficients would get a covariance matrix.”
The issue text states the unexpected return shape: “The `C` return for `jax.numpy.polyfit` when `cov=True, full=False` is always `(n, n, 1)`, regardless of the shape of `y`.”

The fix description and diff show the numerical/broadcasting property needed for correctness: when multiple rhs are present, `fac` (from `resids / (len(x_arr) - order)`) must be expanded/broadcast so that the covariance has one matrix per `rhs` (implemented via `atleast_1d(fac)[np.newaxis, np.newaxis, :]`).
reproduction_risks: Reproduction depends on using `cov=True` with `full=False` and on `y` having multiple right-hand sides (`y` shaped `(M, num_rhs)` with `num_rhs>1`).
The mismatch is about covariance output shape/content per rhs, so using `num_rhs=1` (or `full=True`) will not exercise the failure mode shown in the issue.
The issue’s example uses float32 (`x` is cast to `'float32'`); using other dtypes may change tolerances and exact values.
